summary: Material change since the prior snapshot: Reuters ship-tracking data confirmed Strait of Hormuz commodity-vessel traffic remained severely depressed over the weekend, while Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority expanded its vessel-sanctions list to 77 ships, increasing maritime-access, insurance and freight persistence risk. Reuters also published a Taiwan central-bank poll in which 28 of 31 economists expected the September 17 policy rate to remain at 2%, while three expected a hike to 2.125%. No new U.S., Taiwan or China official macro release was identified since the prior snapshot.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: The risk mix remains adverse for Taiwan equities: U.S. long yields remain near 5%, Reuters-reported market pricing for a September Fed hike increased to about 89%, crude remains around $108 Brent, Hormuz physical-flow and maritime-access constraints remain severe, and Russian refined-product disruption persists. Taiwan's AI/HPC export cycle remains the main offset, while the domestic central-bank base case is still a hold at 2% according to the latest Reuters poll.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market probabilities, intraday market observations, conflict-related supply estimates and economist polls are semantic evidence only and must not overwrite deterministic macro series.

key_drivers.name: Hormuz physical-flow stress remains severe
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported preliminary ship-tracking data showing only four commodity vessels exited and ten entered the Gulf through Hormuz over the weekend, below a 10-day average of about 14 commodity-vessel movements per day; before the Iran war, the strait typically handled about 125 large commercial vessel transits per day. Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority also published an updated list of 77 vessels facing potential penalties for alleged protocol violations.
key_drivers.interpretation: This confirms that the shock remains a physical-flow and maritime-access constraint, increasing persistence risk for tanker availability, insurance, freight, delivered energy and imported inflation.

key_drivers.name: Russia-Ukraine refinery attacks remain a refined-product shock
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported repeated Ukrainian long-range drone strikes have reduced Russian fuel production. President Trump urged Ukraine to stop targeting Russian diesel infrastructure, while Russia downgraded its 2026 oil-output forecast and fuel-export outlook because of the war.
key_drivers.interpretation: The refined-product channel can reinforce freight, inflation and rate pressure independently of Middle East crude disruptions.

key_drivers.name: U.S. inflation and oil keep Fed hike risk elevated
key_drivers.observed: August headline CPI rose 0.4% m/m and 3.4% y/y; core CPI rose 0.3% m/m and 2.4% y/y. Reuters reported CME FedWatch pricing of about 89% for a hike at this week's meeting.
key_drivers.interpretation: Near-5% 10-year yields and renewed energy inflation increase duration pressure on Taiwan technology equities; the market probability is not an official Fed forecast.

key_drivers.name: Taiwan central-bank base case remains hold
key_drivers.observed: A Reuters poll of 31 economists found 28 expected the September 17 policy rate to remain at 2%, while three expected a hike to 2.125%.
key_drivers.interpretation: The domestic policy base case remains unchanged, but a Fed hike and persistent imported-energy inflation could raise the probability of later tightening.

key_risks: A sustained U.S. 10Y yield near 5% and a renewed Fed hiking cycle can compress long-duration semiconductor and AI-hardware valuation multiples.

Persistently depressed Hormuz traffic, direct vessel-security incidents, an expanded Iranian vessel-sanctions list and the Saudi East-West Pipeline outage increase the probability of persistent delivered-energy, freight and insurance-cost pressure.
Russia-Ukraine attacks on refinery infrastructure add a refined-product/diesel shock that can raise trucking, shipping and industrial logistics costs even if crude supply stabilizes.
Taiwan's strong AI/HPC export cycle offsets but does not eliminate energy, FX, rates and global-demand risks.
DXY, VIX, copper and the latest USD/TWD close remain stale in this semantic snapshot because no sufficiently authoritative newer exact value was incorporated.

events.semantic_interpretation: The loss of a near-term diplomatic de-escalation catalyst, combined with unresolved physical supply and shipping constraints, raises the persistence probability of an imported-energy shock.
